events.title: Emperor Xian abdicates, ending the Han dynasty
events.description: Emperor Xian, the last emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty and long a puppet of warlords, was forced to abdicate by Cao Pi, son of Cao Cao. Cao Pi founded the Wei dynasty, opening the Three Kingdoms period.
events.html: Emperor Xian, the last emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty and long a puppet of warlords, was forced to abdicate by Cao Pi, son of Cao Cao. Cao Pi founded the Wei dynasty, opening the Three Kingdoms period.

events.title: Julian enters Constantinople as sole Roman emperor
events.description: Julian entered Constantinople as sole emperor and, despite his rejection of Christianity, presided over the Christian burial of Constantius, escorting the body to the Church of the Apostles. The act demonstrated his lawful right to the throne.
events.html: Julian entered Constantinople as sole emperor and, despite his rejection of Christianity, presided over the Christian burial of Constantius, escorting the body to the Church of the Apostles. The act demonstrated his lawful right to the throne.

events.title: The Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil is assassinated
events.description: Al-Mutawakkil, the tenth Abbasid caliph, was murdered by Turkish military officers. His death began the Anarchy at Samarra, which lasted until 870 and saw four caliphs made and unmade by rival military groups.

events.title: Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas is murdered by John Tzimiskes
events.description: The Byzantine emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, who had retaken Crete and Cyprus and conquered Cilicia, was murdered by his nephew, the general John Tzimiskes, who seized the throne as John I.
events.html: The Byzantine emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, who had retaken Crete and Cyprus and conquered Cilicia, was murdered by his nephew, the general John Tzimiskes, who seized the throne as John I.

events.title: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, last native Prince of Wales, is killed
events.description: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was killed near Cilmeri during Edward I's conquest of Wales. Wales lost its independence, and in 1301 Edward gave the title Prince of Wales to his own son.
events.html: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was killed near Cilmeri during Edward I's conquest of Wales. Wales lost its independence, and in 1301 Edward gave the title Prince of Wales to his own son.

events.title: James II flees London
events.description: As William of Orange advanced, James II slipped out of Whitehall and dropped the Great Seal into the Thames. Caught at Faversham, he escaped to France later that month; Parliament treated his flight as abdication.
events.html: As William of Orange advanced, James II slipped out of Whitehall and dropped the Great Seal into the Thames. Caught at Faversham, he escaped to France later that month; Parliament treated his flight as abdication.

events.title: Louis XVI goes on trial before the National Convention
events.description: The deposed king, now called Louis Capet, appeared before the National Convention to answer charges of treason. He was convicted and guillotined in January 1793.
events.html: The deposed king, now called Louis Capet, appeared before the National Convention to answer charges of treason. He was convicted and guillotined in January 1793.

events.title: Edward VIII abdicates to marry Wallis Simpson
events.description: The abdication took legal effect, and that evening Edward broadcast that he could not reign 'without the help and support of the woman I love'. His brother succeeded as George VI.

events.title: Germany and Italy declare war on the United States
events.description: Four days after Pearl Harbor, Hitler and Mussolini declared war on the United States. The decision brought American power fully into the war in Europe.
